ImageDescription.value: This is Kilkenny Castle, also known as Caisleán Chill Chainnigh, which was built starting in 1195 to control a ford on the River Nore, and was completed in 1213, originally including a large wall that enclosed the entire town of Kilkenny. The structure was started by Richard de Clare, 2nd Earl of Pembroke, and later owned by the Butlers of Ormonde, whom altered and enlarged the castle into the palatial manor house it exists as today, mostly in the 19th Century. The castle was damaged during the Irish Civil War in 1922, and continued to decline until it was sold by James Arthur Butler, 6th Marquess of Ormonde to the Irish State in 1967, after which extensive restoration work was carried out, bringing the castle back to its 19th Century glory.

Credit.value: Castle Gateway, Kilkenny Castle, Cill Chainnigh, Éire

Artist.value: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States

UsageTerms.value: Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication

pages.title: File:Backdrop for opening of Alice Kyteler Festival.jpg

ObjectName.value: Backdrop for opening of Alice Kyteler Festival

Categories.value: Kilkenny Castle|Cartoon Saloon|Self-published work|Uploaded with Mobile/Android|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Photographs taken on 2024-11-01

ImageDescription.value:
Backdrop for opening of Alice Kyteler Festival at Kilkenny Castle. The artwork by Cartoon Saloon depicts Petronilla di Midia (Petronella de Meath) being burnt at the stake on November 3rd 1324. She was the first person to be convicted of witchcraft and burnt at the stake in Ireland. 
A conference was held in her and Alice Kyteler’s memory from November 1st to 3rd in Kilkenny. The keynote speech by Dr. Bernadette Williams was held shortly after this photograph was taken at the Parade Tower of Kilkenny Castle.

DateTimeOriginal.value: 1 November 2024 (according to Exif data)
